clue.text: Perhaps sees Nimrod flying east, east of China

indicators.note: in an across entry, being east of something means coming to its right, after it

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, so a pal

indicators.note: flying suggests letters scattered through the air and landing rearranged

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A traveller notices the biblical hunter Nimrod heading east from China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: the word sees reads the same both ways. China means mate via rhyming slang (china plate). 'flying' scrambles the hunter's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A word spelt identically forwards and backwards is this, and sees is one instance.

clue.text: Work steadily, without a flicker

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for working steadily surrounds the a

parts.note: to ply is to work steadily at a trade or task

explanation.surface: Someone labours on, steady as a candle burning without a flicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: PLY goes round A. The surface makes 'Work' the definition, but the answer is the play of light, a flicker.
explanation.definitionFit: The play of light on water is its shimmering, dancing movement, a flicker.

clue.text: Out of his head, clumsy fool's jump on ice

indicators.note: his head is the first letter of the fool word, and it is put out, removed

parts.note: a klutz is a clumsy, awkward person (US slang)

explanation.surface: A clumsy, crazed skater attempts a jump on the rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of his head' looks like 'mad' but tells you to drop the head (first letter) of KLUTZ.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure-skating leap taking off from the back outside edge of a skate, named after a skater.

clue.text: Thin type of key that makes a squeak

parts.note: narrow means thin, slender
Escape is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A slim key in a lock that squeaks when turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' suggests a door key, but it is the Escape key on a keyboard. A 'narrow squeak' is a close shave.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeak, as in a narrow squeak, is a close call where disaster is only just avoided.

clue.text: Top reserves are telling England stars they could be capped

indicators.note: the top of each of the following words means its initial letter in this down clue

explanation.surface: Reserve players are telling England's star players that they might win caps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capped' suggests sports caps for international players; it is the British practice of rate-capping, a government limit on local property taxes (rates).
explanation.definitionFit: Rates were British local property taxes, and central government could cap, or limit, them.

clue.text: Mine sucks foul grime

indicators.note: foul suggests letters fouled up, tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A coal mine sucks in filthy grime.
explanation.definitionFit: Muckiness is dirtiness, the state of being covered in filth or grime.

clue.text: Not against having female academic

parts.note: pro means in favour of, not against

explanation.surface: An academic who supports women's causes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is short for professor, a senior university academic.

clue.text: Vet nearly bitten by snapping terriers and bigger dogs

indicators.note: bitten by means held between the teeth, inside the other letters
snapping suggests something broken apart and reassembled differently
nearly means the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A vet gets bitten by snappy terriers and larger hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snapping' looks like a description of the terriers' temper, but it is the anagram signal; 'nearly' trims the vet and 'bitten by' sets that inside the scrambled dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrievers are large gun dogs, bigger than most terriers.

clue.text: Given tart, girl and boy produced waffle?

parts.note: a flan is an open tart
Nell is a girl's name
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl and boy, handed a tart, cook up waffles too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waffle' tempts as batter; here it is evasive talk, and to flannel is to talk waffle.
explanation.definitionFit: To flannel is British slang for talking evasively or flatteringly, which is producing waffle.

clue.text: Worker caught in lorry by a very cold place

parts.note: the ant is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for caught inside the lorry word

parts.note: artic is British slang for an articulated lorry
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A labourer is caught in a truck beside a freezing spot.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC is British for an articulated lorry, a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: The southern polar continent is the coldest region on Earth.

clue.text: In Vietnam, potentially a very hot place

indicators.note: in means the answer is found within the letters of the following word

explanation.surface: Vietnam might be a very hot place.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is liable to erupt, so it can become extremely hot at any time.

clue.text: Gain unfair advantage, as speed top is employed to do?

definitions.meaning: to trick or deceive someone for one's own gain

definitions.text: as speed top is employed to do?
definitions.meaning: a whipping top meant for speed is pulled hard on its string to spin it fast

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the idiom literally: a spinning top is set going by pulling its cord, and a fast one is pulled to make it spin rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to deceive or trick, and literally describes yanking a quick spinning top into motion.

clue.text: Guidance system for Old Ironsides

definitions.meaning: the founding principles by which a state is governed
the nickname of the US Navy frigate launched in 1797, still afloat in Boston

explanation.definitionFit: A nation's founding governing principles guide it; USS Constitution is the famous frigate nicknamed Old Ironsides.

clue.text: Frozen plants to cultivate

parts.note: stocks are garden flowers (genus Matthiola)
to till is to cultivate the soil

explanation.surface: Garden flowers frozen in the ground, ready to plough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plants' is plural verb-like but means stocks, a scented garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, as if frozen in place.

clue.text: Revise, spreading different test papers on the table?

indicators.note: the letters are spread out and laid down in a different order

explanation.surface: A student revising lays out different test papers on the desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'papers' and 'table' suggest exam scripts on a desk; they are paper napkins on a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Serviettes are table napkins, often made of paper, laid at each place setting.

clue.text: Strain that's well-known in London police force and Parisian one

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's force
une is French for one (feminine)

explanation.surface: London's police and a Parisian force share a famous tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' suggests stress; here it is a melody, a familiar one tied to a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme tune is a familiar melody associated with a programme or film, a recognised strain of music.

clue.text: 10 climbing, having put unstable high explosive on top to increase risk

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on top means coming first, above what follows
unstable means the letters will not stay in place and are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written before being rearranged

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, the Sicilian volcano

explanation.surface: Someone climbs a volcano with unstable explosive strapped on top, raising the danger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 is a cross-reference to the volcano at 10 across; 'climbing' reads it upwards in this down entry. 'unstable' scrambles put, and 'on top' sets that and the explosive above.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the opening stake, so raising it increases what is at risk.

clue.text: Left guarding front and rear of First Lady's flat

indicators.note: guarding means standing on either side, enclosing the other piece
the abbreviation appears both at the front and at the rear of what it encloses

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A bodyguard leaves to protect the front and back of the President's wife's apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests the US president's wife; here it is Eve, the first woman, with L at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat, even, without slope.

clue.text: Old cardinals from the city

parts.note: cardinal numbers as written in Roman numerals: CIV is 104
Roman numerals again: IC is a form for 99

explanation.surface: Elderly churchmen hailing from the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen; it means cardinal numbers, and 'Old' makes them Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town and its affairs.

clue.text: Request on time by pro-church working group

indicators.note: on means placed next to, following, the time abbreviation

parts.note: to ask is to request
for means in favour of, pro
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A pro-church committee requests more time.
explanation.definitionFit: A task force is a group formed to carry out a particular job.

clue.text: Chelsea caved in after excessive run

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged club after the word for excessive

parts.note: steep means excessive, as a steep price

indicators.note: caved in suggests collapse, letters falling into a new order

explanation.surface: Chelsea football club collapsed after an overlong run of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run' looks like a sporting run of results for the football club, but it is the definition: a race over jumps. 'caved in' scrambles the club's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a race, run over jumps or obstacles.

clue.text: Fuss caused by back-to back houses dominating area

indicators.note: in a down clue, dominating means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house, here one of the houses

indicators.note: back-to-back means the second is turned round to face the first

parts.note: HO again, the other house abbreviation

explanation.surface: Terraced houses built back to back overlook an area and cause a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Back-to-back houses are British terraced housing sharing a rear wall. 'back-to back' turns the second HO into OH; 'dominating' puts both above A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a commotion or fuss.

clue.text: Judge after vacation pockets fine for crack

indicators.note: pockets means takes inside, holding the other piece
vacation empties the word of its middle, leaving the first and last letters

parts.note: OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A judge back from holiday pockets a fine for a wisecrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' suggests a holiday; it empties JUDGE to JE, which 'pockets' OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, a wisecrack.

clue.text: Finally lay to rest, buried by English island

indicators.note: buried by means placed under the English abbreviation in this down entry
finally means the last letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A person is finally laid to rest on an English island.
explanation.walkthrough: An eyot (or ait) is a small island in a river, common on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small river island.

clue.text: Shred letter from overseas

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not a shred
a character of the Greek alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny amount, as in not one jot; also the ninth Greek alphabet letter.

clue.text: In which one may study cricket?

definitions.text: In which one may study cricket?

parts.words: In which one may study cricket?
parts.note: cricket seems the bat-and-ball game, but here it is the chirping insect, the subject of a branch of zoology

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is the English bat-and-ball game; the clue means the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This field is the scientific study of insects, such as crickets.

clue.text: Get rid of topless drunk

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to flush out is to get rid of

explanation.surface: Throw out the topless drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is a heavy drinker, a drunk.

clue.text: Lowering end of rope into opening of dark cellar

indicators.note: into means put inside the other letters
opening of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: a basement is a cellar

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lowering a rope's end into the mouth of a dark cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Debasement is a degrading or reduction in value or quality, a lowering.
